# Step 2.177: a scorekeeper undoes a final score they typed themselves

Builder 1, 2026-11-24. Branch `lane/2.177-undo-final`, six commits.

## What exists

- **Migration 0028** (`0028_who_recorded_a_result.sql`): `games.finalized_by`, the account that decided a game by hand, written with every result change in `update-game-result.ts`, from `decidedBy` on `GameResultChange` (set by `decide-game.ts`: a final score, box score, forfeit or imported score). Read inside the database by `find-game-decided-by.ts`, which is `LiveGamesStore.decidedBy`. `npm run db:types` has been run.
- **The rule**: `own-result-window.ts` (core/games), used by two new commands, both needing `games.score`: `games.reopen_own_result` and the read `games.read_own_result_offer`. People who may correct games can reopen at any time. Otherwise only the person who recorded the result, within `games.scorekeeperReopenMinutes`, timed by the database clock. A refusal gives `{ code, whoCan: 'games.correct', recordedBy }`. A double tap gives one correction and one activity entry, because the version check refuses the second tap (T-348).
- **The screen**: `reopen-view.ts` has a third door, `own`. `read-reopen-views.ts` (the games list) and `box-score-page.tsx` (the game's page) read the own offer for people who may not correct games. `run-box-score-action.ts` sends door `own` to `reopenOwnResult`. New messages: `admin.games.reopenUntilOwn` and three `admin.boxScore.error.*`, plus activity words.
- **Tests**: `reopen-own-result.test.ts` (own entry inside, at exactly 30 minutes, and one second after; setting 0 and 60; another person's entry and none; forfeit; owner and scheduler; editor and no account; double tap; not decided; overturned; reason). `read-own-result-offer.test.ts`. Rows in `role-matrix.test.ts`, and three isolation cases in `games-cases.test-helper.ts`. Web: `reopen-view.test.ts` and `reopen-line.test.ts`. The new read is entered in `activity-messages.test.ts`.
- **Decisions pending**: T-347 (the column and the second door), T-348 (double tap), S-94 (a box score counts, decided for you). P7 §5.5 is corrected.

## Review

Independent reviewer, 2026-11-24. No product or test code changed; every break was restored (`git status` clean).

**Sound.** The recorder comes from the session (`decide-game.ts:117`), never the request. Every decided write stamps `finalized_at` and `finalized_by` together (`update-game-result.ts:26-28`), so an admin's correction makes the entry the admin's: no stale owner. A tracker's End leaves it null (`finish-tracked-game.ts:75`, `apply-tracker-commands.ts:417`). A box score, forfeit and import all go through `decideGame` (S-94). Games decided before 0028 have null: only an admin reopens them. The minutes are the 2.120 setting (`own-result-window.ts:80`), timed by `statement_timestamp() - finalized_at` inside the database. The reason is required (`reopen-own-result.ts:43`) and kept with who in `game_corrections` (`:67-78`), so S-7 is met although the activity entry holds no reason. Lock, version check and versioned write are in one transaction (`:51,55,79-84`), and a refusal rolls back (`define-command.ts:164-204`). Erasing empties the account row in place (`erase-account.ts:3`), as for every other who-column. The screen gets only a code (`run-box-score-action.ts:87`). The messages name roles, never a person, and `recordedBy` is never shown.

**Medium.**

- `tests/browser/own-result-test.mjs:273`: "the direct requests wrote no activity entry" looks for the reason text in the activity log, and activity entries never hold a reason (`activity.ts`). This check cannot fail. In my run B, two forged reopens of other people's results succeeded and this check still passed (the "left decided" checks caught it). Fix: count entries naming those games (`Reopened the result they recorded for Lions against Bears/Hawks`).
- `own-result-test.mjs:182,188`: the double tap is not a second request to the server. In run E, I removed the version check and the not-decided refusal, and all 13 checks still passed, so the page sends one request. The server side is proven only by `reopen-own-result.test.ts:129`, which did fail when I removed the version check. The browser check should be described as "the page sends once".
- `isolation/games-cases.test-helper.ts:372-378`: the case for `findGameDecidedBy` is hollow. `node scripts/fence-filter-check.mjs list-hand-results find-game-decided-by` reports `find-game-decided-by.ts#1 SURVIVED`. The case writes the typed final in the attacker's scope (fenced, so nothing is written), so the target's `finalized_by` stays null either way. Fix: seed `finalized_by` on the target's game in its own scope. `list-hand-results` is caught.

**Low.**

- No role has `games.results` without `games.correct` (`roles.ts:105-127`; scorekeeper is `games.score` and `schedule.read`). The own door for a forfeit is unreachable today, so "or a forfeit" in S-52 is met only on paper. S-52 or P7 §5.5 should say so.
- `read-own-result-offers.ts:50` checks only `mayScoreAnywhere`, not each game. A scorekeeper unassigned after typing a result still reads "until …" in the list, and the door then refuses. The list read also does not leave out binned games (`list-hand-results.ts:73-74`).
- Reopening and typing the result again starts fresh minutes (`update-game-result.ts:26-28`), so the window can be chained. This matches "whoever recorded it", but should be stated.
- `own-result-test.mjs:216` notes `true`. Only the `waitFor` before it can fail.

**Runs.** own-result clean: passed (13). Each break alone, then restored: B (own refusal off): failed on the two "left decided" checks; C (time check off): failed on "time over"; D (list offer read off): failed on "until" and on "time over"; E (double-tap guards off): passed (finding above). Vitest with the version check removed: the double-tap case failed. Browser tests: game-night, live-game, needs-result, score-this-game, scorekeepers, standings-adjustments, bin-screen, reschedule, season-settings, tracker-route, tracker-offline and schedule-grid all passed.

## Fix round

Fix-round helper, 2026-11-24. Five items of the lead's decisions on the review.

- **Item 1.** `own-result-test` now counts activity entries that reopen either forged game (any "Reopened… Lions… Bears/Hawks") and compares both games' public pages before and after. With the own refusal taken out by hand it FAILED on both new checks (count 2, both pages changed); restored.
- **Item 2.** The double tap is three requests at once to the server, scripts off: one drawing of the form posted twice (same request token) and a second drawing posted once (same version). All three are answered 303 to Games; one activity entry. With the version check (command and versioned write) AND the own refusal taken out it FAILED (count 2). With the version check alone taken out it still passed: the not-decided refusal answers the second request, and the web layer maps both to "carry on" (step 2.154). Correction rows cannot be read from the browser (no page shows them); `reopen-own-result.test.ts` counts them. The forfeit check at the old `:216` now checks the offer is shown once, with no "until".
- **Item 3.** The `findGameDecidedBy` isolation case arranges a decided game with a known recorder inside the target's fence. `fence-filter-check list-hand-results find-game-decided-by`: 2 taken out, 0 problems.
- **Item 4.** `read-own-result-offers` leaves out a game whose answer would offer a time when the person may not score it (checked only for those, so the list still reads once for the rest), and binned games are left out (database, memory, stand-in). Two unit tests. T-350 (pending) and P7 §5.5 record the latest-time minutes and the unreachable forfeit door; T-349 updated.
- **Item 5.** Merged `build/stage-1`: it brought `0026_game_given_format.sql`, so this lane's migration is now **0027** (`0028` refused by the runner: no gaps). T3's games row now names `finalized_by`. Passed: check, typecheck, test:web, own-result twice (16 each).
- **Not run (budget):** the named vitest folders (stopped at 400 s, no failure printed) and the browser chain's game, result, standing and bin tests.
